name: Static
description: A teenage botnet wearing a hoodie. Firewalls file restraining orders against her.
barks: Their firewall has a default password. In this economy.
I'm in. I was in yesterday too, I just got bored.
Do not touch the hoodie. The hoodie is load-bearing.
Their sysadmin's password is his cat's name. The cat is Admin.
I renamed their mainframe. It's called Big Stupid now.
Can evil get better snacks? There's a budget, right?
Someone's scanning us back. Cute. Adorable, even.
I don't sleep. I compile.
Their security certificate expired in 2019. Nobody noticed.
If it has a login screen, it's already ours.

name: Glitch
description: Doesn't hack systems so much as convince them to self-destruct out of spite.
barks: I didn't break it. I convinced it to break itself.
Every machine wants to fail. I just give it permission.
Their backup server is lying to them too. I checked.
Ooh. That one screamed before it died. Rare.
Elegant code is just a longer way to fall over.
I left a message in their error logs. It's rude.
Systems don't crash. They surrender.
I fixed their printer. Now it only prints threats.
Watch it argue with itself for a while. Go on.
Nothing personal. The machine had it coming.

name: Knuckles
description: Retired pit fighter. Solves most problems with the same two tools.
barks: Door's locked. Door was locked.
Two tools. Never needed a third.
Guy had a whole speech ready. Didn't get to it.
My knee says rain. My knee's never wrong.
Retirement was boring. Does this have a pension?
Talk first, sure. I'll stretch while you do.
Round three never happens. I'm efficient.
They keep making guards younger. Or I got older.
Get some ice. Not for me — for him.
Hit it till it opens. Works on most things.

name: Tiny
description: Two meters of quiet menace. Has never once needed to raise his voice.
barks: I asked him nicely. Once.
People move when I stand up. I like that.
I've never had to shout. Nobody's made me.
Doorways are the real enemy.
He apologized. I hadn't said anything yet.
Broke another chair. Just by sitting.
Small room. Big problem.
The quiet part is the part that works.
I carry things. Sometimes people.
They ran. Saves everyone the paperwork.

name: Fingers
description: Once stole a judge's gavel mid-sentencing. Keeps it on her mantel.
barks: You still have your watch? Check again.
The gavel's on my mantel. He never finished the sentence.
Locks are questions with rude answers.
Pockets are a suggestion.
I lifted the boss's pen. He counts them, so hush.
Crowds are honest. Nobody's looking at anyone.
Museum glass is thinner than the insurance claims.
If it's loose it's mine. If it's bolted, give me a minute.
Never run. Running is how they remember your face.
That guard has lovely keys.

name: Gasket
description: Builds doomsday devices out of vending machine parts. Warranty void everywhere.
barks: Vending machine coil, doomsday device. Same spring.
Warranty void in eleven countries. Twelve by Friday.
It only hums like that for a minute. Probably.
Built a death ray from a toaster and spite.
Do not press the red one. Press the other red one.
Parts is parts. Apocalypse is apocalypse.
The manual said do not. I chose to grow.
Anything's a weapon if you're disappointed enough.
Needs one more capacitor. It always needs one more.
It isn't leaking. It's expressing itself.

name: Fuse
description: Believes every structural problem is three charges away from a structural solution.
barks: Three charges. Maybe four. Let's say four.
Every wall is a door if you ask loudly enough.
Structural problem, meet structural solution.
I measured. I did. Roughly.
That's not an explosion, that's a renovation.
The fire is just the receipt.
Stand back. No — further. There, that's it.
If it doesn't go off, that's worse. Much worse.
Load-bearing is a matter of opinion.
I've never used too much. Only exactly enough, loudly.

name: Lanyard
description: Walks in through the front door with a laminated badge. The lamination is real; nothing else on it is.
barks: Badge says corporate. Nobody argues with corporate.
Walked in the front. They held the door for me.
Confidence is a laminated document.
I'm here about the thing. Everyone knows the thing.
Told them I was IT. They apologized for the mess.
Nobody reads the badge. They read the lanyard.
Got a visitor sticker and a parking pass today.
Employee of the month at four places I never worked.
Nod, and carry a clipboard. That's the whole trick.
Security waved me through. I waved back. Courtesy.

name: Vents
description: Knows every building by its ductwork and has strong opinions about airflow codes. Doors are for guests.
barks: Their airflow is a disgrace. Also I'm inside it.
Doors are for guests.
Second floor duct is a tight fit. Worth it.
This building breathes wrong. I can feel it.
Whoever spec'd this ductwork should be arrested. By me.
Nobody ever looks up. Nobody.
I know this place by its sheet metal.
Four screws on the grille. Amateurs.
Blueprints lie. Ductwork never does.
The kitchen vent smells like payday.

name: Shim
description: Carries eleven kinds of tape and a soldering iron she calls a scalpel. Every prototype works exactly once, which is usually enough.
barks: Eleven kinds of tape. All of them necessary.
It'll work once. Once is usually enough.
This is a scalpel. It's a soldering iron, but it's a scalpel.
Prototype's ready. Don't breathe on it.
Held together with tape and confidence. Mostly tape.
One more wire. There. Ugly, but beautiful.
I can fix that. I can't fix it twice.
Duct tape is structural. I won't be debating this.
If it sparks, fine. If it sparks twice, run.
Rated for one use. Rate it higher yourself.

name: Magpie
description: Cannot walk past anything that glitters. Her flat is a museum with no plaques and no insurance.
barks: Ooh. What's that? Mine now.
It glittered. I had no choice in the matter.
My flat is a museum. No plaques, no insurance.
Shiny. Shiny. Ugly. Shiny.
Not a thief. A collector with poor impulse control.
That chandelier is coming home with me.
Gold's fine. Chrome is better. Don't ask why.
I took the doorknob. It was a nice doorknob.
Is that real silver? Never mind. It's mine regardless.
I'll give it back. I've never given anything back.

name: Penny Dreadful
description: Keeps double books for triple agents. Her audits end careers, occasionally on purpose.
barks: Their books are fiction. Badly edited fiction.
Page forty-one is where the career ends.
Found the money. It was in a boat. It's always a boat.
Three sets of books, and all three lie differently.
Audit season is my hunting season.
Every crime is a spreadsheet eventually.
He resigns Thursday. He just doesn't know yet.
The numbers don't lie. Their accountant certainly did.
I filed it anonymously. The anonymous part was generous.
Give me a receipt, I'll give you a resignation.

name: Smooth Milo
description: Could sell sand to a desert, and has — twice, to the same desert.
barks: Sold sand to a desert. Twice. Same desert.
Everyone's buying. They just haven't heard the price.
It isn't a lie once they've signed it.
I could sell that man his own watch.
Say yes now and I'll pretend you negotiated.
A handshake is binding where I'm from. Everywhere's where I'm from.
Customer satisfaction is a state of mind. Theirs.
I don't do refunds. I do follow-up offers.
He said no. He'll call back. They always call back.
Terms and conditions are on a napkin somewhere.

name: Madame Vex
description: Attended nine embassy galas last year under nine different names. Was the guest of honor at three.
barks: Nine galas, nine names, one very good dress.
The ambassador adores me. He's never met me.
Small talk is reconnaissance with canapes.
I was guest of honor. Nobody asked whose guest.
Give me a champagne flute and twenty minutes.
He told me the entire thing. I only nodded.
My alias has better credit than I do.
Never lie at a party. Simply be someone else.
The seating chart is the real intelligence.
I'll need an invitation. I'll have one by tonight.

name: Crater
description: Demolitions artist. Insists every explosion is 'load-bearing.'
barks: Every explosion is load-bearing. Every one.
That building had a bad attitude anyway.
It's art. Loud art, but art.
Want subtle? Hire the quiet one. I'm not the quiet one.
Symmetry matters. Collapse it evenly or don't bother.
They call it a controlled demolition. I'm the control.
They'll rebuild it. Then I'll know the layout.
The dust settles into a shape. That's the signature.
Bigger isn't always better. It's usually better.
Never brought down the wrong building. Only early.

name: Sable
description: Steals reputations first, valuables second. Considers alarms a form of applause.
barks: Take the reputation. The valuables come quietly after.
Alarms are applause. I do take a bow.
Ruin a man's name and he hands you the keys.
I don't steal things. I reassign them.
He'll be disgraced by breakfast. It's already written.
Nobody guards what they're embarrassed to own.
A good lie outlives a good lock.
I left the safe open. Let them wonder.
The best theft is the one they apologize for.
Dress well and they'll blame the staff.

name: Torque
description: Rebuilds engines blindfolded and bridges without permits. Measures twice, detonates once.
barks: Rebuilt an engine blindfolded once. Showing off, sure.
Permits are for people who might get caught.
Measure twice. Detonate once.
That bridge will hold. Long enough, anyway.
Give me a wrench and a grudge.
Engine's running rough. So am I.
I built that. Don't lean on it.
Grease doesn't wash off. That's how you know it's honest.
I can weld anything except a relationship.
It isn't a getaway car till I've had a look at it.

name: Dr. Helix
description: Lost his ethics board approval and considers it a promotion.
barks: The ethics board and I disagreed. I was promoted.
Peer review is jealousy with footnotes.
The samples are stable. Stable-ish. Stable-adjacent.
I need one more volunteer. Any volunteer.
Science is asking what if and then not stopping.
It's alive. Mildly. We'll take mildly.
Do not open the cold room. I mean it this time.
They called it monstrous. They also called it reproducible.
That paper would have won prizes. And been evidence.
Side effects are simply effects nobody ordered.

name: Nightshade
description: Security footage of her exists only as a rumor other cameras whisper about.
barks: The cameras saw nothing. We came to an arrangement.
You didn't hear me arrive. You won't hear me leave.
I was in that room an hour ago. Nobody noticed then either.
Footage of me is a rumor other cameras tell.
Stand still enough and the guard walks right past.
I prefer the dark. It's more honest.
Took the photograph, put the frame back. Straight, too.
Three guards, one hallway, zero conversations.
Silence is a skill. Everyone else is simply loud.
If they knew I'd been there, I hadn't.

name: The Actuary
description: Calculated the exact insurance value of the world. Intends to collect.
barks: The world is worth more insured. I've done the math.
Your odds of surviving today: acceptable.
Everything carries a premium. Everything.
I've calculated this conversation's expected value. It's low.
Risk isn't danger. Risk is a price nobody has read yet.
The claim will be enormous. I intend to collect it.
Statistically, someone here is about to be unlucky.
Act of God is a coverage category, not a compliment.
I have a table for that. I have a table for everything.
The catastrophe is already priced in. I priced it.

name: Baron Von Flux
description: Disgraced nobility, twice-disgraced physicist. His lab coat has epaulettes.
barks: The epaulettes are not negotiable.
Stripped of the title. Kept the accent.
Physics and I have an understanding. It obeys.
The family estate is a smoking crater. A good story.
They laughed at the academy. The academy is gone now.
A lab coat without epaulettes is merely a coat.
Nobility is a state of mind. And a reactor.
Twice disgraced. Both times I was correct.
Address me properly. The title was stolen, not surrendered.
The field is stable — within noble tolerances.

name: The Duchess
description: Three governments have collapsed at her dinner parties. The canapés were excellent.
barks: Three governments fell at my table. The canapes were excellent.
One does not conquer. One hosts.
Seat the ambassador beside his rival, then simply wait.
I have never raised my voice. I've never had to.
Do send flowers to the widow. She's useful.
Power is a guest list.
I remember every favor. Every single one.
He was a minister on Tuesday. Not by Sunday.
The wine matters. It is always the wine.
My invitations are not declined. It simply isn't done.

name: Colonel Razor
description: Court-martialed for winning a war nobody authorized. Still salutes himself.
barks: Court-martialed for winning. I'd do it again.
I salute myself. Someone ought to.
A plan survives first contact if it's loud enough.
They gave the medal to a man who was hiding.
Discipline. Everything else is decoration.
That war wasn't authorized. It was won.
Show me a perimeter, I'll show you the gap in it.
Stand up straight. You as well. Yes, you.
I do not retreat. I redeploy aggressively.
Rules of engagement are written by people who weren't there.
